newsitem.title: USA: CME hog and pork bellies called steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hog and pork bellies called steady to higher.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent higher, analysts said.

Carryover demand in hog futures is expected to stem from storm reduced hog runs and steady to higher cash hog indications. Heavy snowfall in the northern Corn Belt should prompt packers to pay up for hogs despite cutouts being in the red, the analysts said.
But gains will be limited by ideas those hogs will come to market later in the week when the weather is expected to clear, they said.
The latest CME lean hog index was off $0.84 at $76.35 per cwt.

The light pace of hog slaughter recently and calls for a reduced hog kill again Tuesday is expected to stimulate carryover support in pork belly futures. But gains will be limited by the recent weak undertone to cash pork bellies, they said.
Evening up is also likely ahead of the weekly CME out-of-town storage report Tuesday afternoon.
Early estimates on the report point to an in-movement of 250,000 to 500,000 lbs versus out 194,000 lbs last week.
